newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta call money stable at 15.0/16.0 percent.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta call money stable at 15.0/16.0 percent.

text.p: Jakarta call money was stable at 15.0/16.0 percent on Tuesday morning, dealers said.
"Liquidity seemed to be okay but many operators were still holding back," one Japanese bank dealer said.
He said rupiah supply was sufficient but not ample.
"It should be enough for the market today, with the help of an early injection of 274 billion rupiah," the dealer said.

Dealers were initially worried over possible tight liquidity due to weekly tax payments and the end of the liquidity reporting period. One state bank dealer said much of the tax payments had been paid last Friday, which helped ease pressure.
One local bank dealer said expensive short-dated swap rates continued to keep overnight money high.
He said operators appeared to be focusing on upcoming Friday liquidity on the assumption that the Friday phenomenon of tight conditions could be repeated again this week.
Another dealer said one-week money was slightly higher at 15.25/15.50 percent but one-month money was well offered at around 14.50/15.00 percent.
The average overnight interbank rate on Monday was 16.01 percent, compared with 21.98 percent last Friday.
